- Ensure compliance with local and international financial reporting standards, and local laws and regulations on
financial related areas

Stakeholder Communication
- Communicate financial information effectively to non-finance stakeholders
- Provide financial insights and recommendations to support strategic decision-making
- Build and maintain relationships with external partners, such as banks, vendors, tax agents and auditors
Experience
- Minimum 15 years' experience in accounting in the manufacturing sector, with at least 8 years in managerial
capacity
- Strong cost accounting knowledge and several years of working closely with the operations team in a factory are
essential
- Strong command of the English language
- High proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint for data analysis and presentations
- Able to lead the finance team and work with other departments to implement applications and/or improve
processes.
- Proven expertise in financial planning, analysis, and budgeting processes.
- Excellent problem-solving and decision-making skills with a strategic mindset.

Product Manager — WMS & Warehouse Integrations
Remote · full time
Why this role exists
The client is an AI-powered fulfilment and logistics ecosystem built for fast-growing e-commerce brands. From one
platform, merchants run global fulfilment, cross-border shipping, and AI logistics intelligence, with AI reducing
errors, lowering costs, and continuously optimising fulfilment and shipping as they scale globally. The ecosystem is
deliberately flexible: the client operates its own WMS for the warehouses it works with, and connects partner
warehouses and external WMS systems through the same platform.
Warehouse-side demand is growing fast: fulfilment accounts, white-label deals, and WMS-shaped RFPs from
prospects. The WMS domain now needs one dedicated owner: our own WMS, the partner WMS integrations, and
the Fulfillment API contract that connects any warehouse to the platform.
Scope of ownership
- All WMS product work, end to end: roadmap, PRDs, sizing with engineers, sprint delivery, QA of WMS flows.
- The whole WMS domain, current and future: our own WMS, partner warehouses and their WMS systems, and
the evaluation of new WMS partners or a next-generation in-house build.
- WMS delivery management day to day: integration specs, sync reliability (WMS to OMS inventory mirrors), bug
escalations with evidence, release coordination with the warehouse and the WMS development team.
- Warehouse-flavoured commercial support: WMS RFP gap analyses and feasibility answers for Sales on "can
the warehouse do X".
What the job is day to day
- Turn warehouse and fulfilment asks into scoped, sized cards engineers can pick up, and run them through the
two-week sprint cadence.
- Own inbound/outbound/inventory flows: receiving orders, pick-pack, dispatch, returns, carton and serial-number
handling, and inventory reconciliation between WMS and OMS.
- Manage the WMS development team hands-on: reproduce issues, bring log and database evidence rather than
symptoms, push for root-cause fixes over per-record patches, and keep a written record of every open issue and
commitment.
- Sit between warehouse operators, the WMS development team, merchants, and the client's engineers, and
keep all four aligned in writing.
- QA the flows yourself before they ship.
Requirements
- 3+ years product management on logistics, fulfilment, warehouse, or supply-chain software (WMS, OMS, 3PL
platform, or adjacent).
- Has shipped integration-heavy product: APIs, webhooks, vendor systems, data sync between platforms.
- Technical fluency: can read a technical spec and hold their own in an engineering discussion about states,
syncs, and edge cases.
- Evidence-first working style: verifies against logs, data, and code before asserting; claims come with proof
attached.
- Clear, structured written English documentation.
- Self-sufficient operator: runs the WMS scope end to end without needing day-to-day direction. Escalates
decisions, not tasks.
- Collaboration fit: works transparently, decisions recorded in writing, no silo-building.
Nice-to-haves
- Direct WMS vendor-management experience, from the implementation side or the vendor side.
- Has run warehouse ops or worked physically close to a warehouse floor.
- Has run a build-vs-buy evaluation or vendor RFP process before.
- Uses AI tools as a working method (specs, QA planning, analysis), not just chat.
- Written Chinese (strong plus: warehouse operations and the WMS development team communicate in Chinese).
Reporting and interfaces
- WMS priorities are set together within the product roadmap with the team.
- Works daily with: platform engineers, the WMS development team, warehouse partners, BD on
warehouse-shaped deals, and CS on fulfilment escalations, and with the owners of adjacent scopes wherever a

WMS change integrates with shipping, billing, or the merchant app.
First 90 days (success looks like)
- Owns our WMS, its development-team relationship, and the WMS-to-OMS inventory-sync reliability queue
outright, as the single point of contact.
- Ships one warehouse-side improvement end to end through the sprint process, including dry-run and warehouse
sign-off.
- Delivers the WMS platform recommendation (evolve our current WMS, adopt a new partner, or build
next-generation in-house), with an evaluated shortlist and evidence.
- Produces the WMS integration playbook: how a new warehouse or vendor gets connected, with gates and tests,
built on the Fulfillment API contract.
- Is the person Sales routes every "can the warehouse do X" question to.
